newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei seen falling, but bottom at 20,200.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei seen falling, but bottom at 20,200.

text.p: Tokyo's key stock index is expected to fall sharply on Thursday, discouraged by the sell-off in U.S. Dow industrials overnight, brokers said.
But they said they expected the index to be supported slightly above the key 20,000 level.
On Wednesday, the Nikkei 225 average closed down 253.74 points, or 1.22 percent, at 20,568.38. Its December futures were down 220 points at 20,570 by the day's end.
"I expect the Nikkei average to slide to as low as 20,200, around the level where last Friday's plunge was supported," said Akishige Ishikura, analyst at Dai-Ichi Securities Co Ltd.
Many brokers said that the key Nikkei average was not likely to fall below the psychological support at 20,000.
When the Nikkei tumbled more than 650 points last Friday, the fall stopped at 20,171.69.
On Wednesday, the nervous U.S. stock market was hit by a variety of unsubstantiated rumours. Dow industrials lost 71 points or 1.09 percent to about 6403 after falling nearly 130 points earlier.
The Nikkei's December futures also tumbled overnight in Chicago.
The December finished at 20,350 on Wednesday, down 410 points from its previous close in Chicago. It was down 220 points from its Osaka close on Wednesday.
Brokers said the Tokyo market was also vulnerable ahead of the settlement of December futures and options on Friday.
